topic: Pete Buttigieg and the fuel-economy rollback
brand: Buttigieg and the fuel rule · 10 facts
caption: "pete buttigieg" — 1,000+ searches today. His department's fuel rule was just rolled back.

Why: On September 28, the Trump administration cut the 2031 fuel-economy target to 34.9 mpg, from the Biden-era 50.4. It says new cars will cost about $1,300 less. Its own estimate says drivers will pay about $1,600 more for gas over a car's life. On NPR, Buttigieg said less innovation will "help hand that advantage to China."

What most people don't know: the fine for missing the target has been $0 since July 4, 2025, when the One Big Beautiful Bill Act zeroed it. Carmakers had paid over $1.1 billion in fines for 2011 to 2020 models.
Very simply put: Monday's rollback lowered a bar that already had no penalty.
